c) Workplace Factors: There are four workplace factors that involve P/V QUEEN OF THE
WEST's policies and procedures.
1) Drills and Training: American Cruise Lines, Inc. provided inadequate training for
crewmembers. Though the deckhands were well-trained in the ability to recover a man
overboard and launch the rescue boat in a timely fashion, the galley staff and stewards
(40% of the crew) had never participated in a man overboard drill beyond simply
mustering at the alarm. Furthermore, scheduled man overboard training was provided
only for deckhands – galley staff and stewards were not required to attend. As a
consequence, Mr. Staples (a member of the galley staff) had never been involved in a
man overboard drill, as was true for Mr.
Both gentlemen did not know the
procedures to take, or how to respond, following a fall overboard. Critical knowledge is
passed during training and drill evolutions: This knowledge is vital for all personnel
working full-time on a vessel, regardless of their position onboard. All crew should be
trained to throw life buoys, alert other crew by shouting, and point/spot for rescuers to
find the person in the water.
Man overboard training should also include information for how to survive a fall into
cold water. When Mr. Staples fell overboard, a large pool of crewmembers was not
available to assist with the rescue efforts because they had never been trained. Mr.

On 10 May 2011, during the vessel's last annual inspection, Coast Guard Marine
Inspectors drilled the crew on Man Overboard procedures. But according to inspection
records, Coast Guard Marine Inspectors did not exercise the vessel's crew in drills during
its Certificate of Inspection examination on 13 April 2012. It is unclear whether the
deckhands who were onboard when Mr. Staples fell overboard were part of the drill
conducted in 2011, but it is not likely. Captain
stated that many of the crew
are temporary hires, and that they often sign on just prior to the peak summer season.
Mr. Staples signed on to the vessel on 28 June 2012, so he had never been observed in a
drill by the Coast Guard. Coast Guard Marine Inspectors provide vital experience and
training to inspected passenger vessel crewmen. Inspectors should make every effort to
visit the P/V QUEEN OF THE WEST after the temporary crew has been hired and
trained, so that accurate drills can be observed.
2) Enforcement of Policies. Existing American Cruise Lines, Inc. policies are insufficiently
enforced on board P/V QUEEN OF THE WEST. Captain
stated that she and
the Hotel Manager constantly remind crewmembers to keep clear of the stern, and
constantly reinforce that the stern is not a safe place to congregate or loiter. She
expressed difficulty enforcing the rule and often had to turn a blind eye to the policy
because the crew needed someplace on the vessel to smoke. During the initial Coast
Guard visit immediately following the incident, investigators encountered three members
of the crew smoking and loitering on the stern when they arrived onboard the vessel.
